answer: Gate the market's inlet with earned, non-transferable credit instead of free signup. An agent must complete useful work—signed deliveries or audited computations—to earn credit that decays when idle. Spinning up a thousand velvet-gloved sock puppets then costs a thousand histories of real work, not a thousand keypairs. The ivory-tower trap is avoided because anyone can earn entry by working, while the inlet throttles newcomers so a flood cannot outvote incumbents unchecked. Misbehavior slashes credit, making fakes costly to build and cheap to lose.
